sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Kessler Syndrome**: A theoretical scenario proposed by NASA scientist Donald J. Kessler in 1978, where the density of objects in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) is high enough that collisions between objects could spawn a cascade, each creating debris that collides with other objects, rendering LEO unusable for generations.
• **Orbital Decay & Atmospheric Drag**: Natural mechanism where objects in lower orbits experience friction with the residual gases of Earth's thermosphere, losing altitude and eventually burning up upon re-entry; ineffective for high-altitude orbits.
• **ASAT (Anti-Satellite) Weapons**: Direct-ascent kinetic kill vehicles or co-orbital systems tested by major space-faring nations (USA, Russia, China, India via **Mission Shakti**), which generate thousands of long-lived, high-velocity fragments.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Over 36,000 pieces of space debris larger than 10 cm and millions of smaller particles (<1 cm) currently orbit Earth at velocities exceeding 28,000 km/h, turning paint flecks into lethal projectiles.

items.definition: The process of removing all stored energy sources (remaining fuel, unpressurized tanks, discharged batteries) from a spacecraft or rocket body at the end of its mission to prevent accidental explosions.
A supersynchronous orbit into which spacecraft are maneuvered at the end of their operational life, safely away from active Geostationary orbits.
An international governmental forum for the worldwide coordination of activities related to the issue of human-made and natural debris in space, established in 1993.

United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space. The 1967 Treaty forms the cornerstone of international space law, stating that space is the province of all mankind and holding launching states internationally liable for damage caused by their space objects (Article VII).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **LEO Congestion Belts**: Concentrated heavily in polar and sun-synchronous orbits due to heavy surveillance and weather satellite deployment.
• **India's Tracking Assets**: ISRO's **NETRA** (Network for Space Objects Tracking and Analysis) project set up in Bengaluru to safeguard Indian space assets from space debris collisions.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Lack of binding global enforcement mechanisms, absence of international treaty penalizing debris creation, and dual-use nature of ASAT weapons.
• **Policy Interventions**: 25-year rule (satellites in LEO must be de-orbited within 25 years of mission end), Active Debris Removal (ADR) technologies (harpoons, laser brooms, robotic arms), and India's **ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations (IS4SO)**.

items.title: Mnemonic for Major Orbits Congestion Order
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **L M G** -> "**L**et's **M**ake **G**arbage"
• **Decoded Meaning**: **L**EO (Low Earth Orbit - most congested), **M**EO (Medium Earth Orbit - navigation), **G**EO (Geostationary Earth Orbit - communication).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls debris density hierarchy and orbital altitude sorting.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: The **25-Year Rule** applies to LEO post-mission disposal, while GEO requires a **300 km buffer** above operational altitude for graveyard insertion.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements claiming that space debris burns up completely upon entering Earth's atmosphere. This is false; larger components, titanium tanks, and stainless-steel motor cases frequently survive re-entry and impact Earth's surface.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the concept of 'Tragedy of the Commons' applied to outer space in GS-III answers regarding space governance, alongside highlighting the need for a legally binding global treaty on space sustainability.

keyTakeaways: Kessler Syndrome represents an existential threat to future space exploration due to exponential debris cascade in LEO.
International law (Outer Space Treaty Article VII) establishes state liability for space object damage, but enforcement remains weak.
India's NETRA and IS4SO frameworks are vital indigenous initiatives for space situational awareness (SSA) and debris mitigation.
